public_rationale: On March 16, 2026, BIS described AI infrastructure financing arrangements involving private credit firms [e1]. At its April 14, 2026 briefing, the IMF described pension and insurer holdings of private credit as fairly manageable in aggregate [e2]. Neither source establishes broad failure of the planned build-out, US$200 billion in unrecovered investment, or the claimed funding share of those losses [e1, e2]. The financing links alone do not settle the conditional forecast [e1, e2].
limitations: The relevant project cohort and final deadline are unspecified.
The evidence does not establish the broad construction-failure condition.
General financing exposure does not measure construction losses after recoveries or trace those losses to pension, retirement, and insurance capital.
The claim supplies no accounting basis or numerical threshold for the private-credit share.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If the planned data centers are not built, hundreds of billions of dollars will have been wasted, much of it private credit backed by pensions and insurance funds.
conditions: if the data centers don't get built

statement.excerpt: And if they don’t get built, hundreds of billions of dollars have been wasted, with large swaths of those billions funded by private credit, which in turn is funded by pensions, retirements and insurance funds.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: hundreds of billions of dollars have been wasted
large swaths of those billions funded by private credit
funded by pensions, retirements and insurance funds
our_interpretation: The antecedent concerns failure to deliver the planned AI data-center build-out discussed in the post. A temporary delay or an isolated cancellation does not by itself establish that broad condition.
The ordinary reading of 'wasted' is unrecovered investment attributable to failed construction, after recoveries and redeployment, rather than announced project value or financing commitments.
I read 'hundreds of billions' as at least US$200 billion in aggregate losses. This numerical floor and the currency identification are evaluator interpretations.
The financing clause requires a substantial share of those same losses to involve private credit traceable to pension, retirement, and insurance capital. The speaker supplies no numerical share.
The surrounding phrase 'the next few years' provides a rough time frame but no unambiguous final date. I therefore assign no fixed deadline.
No accounting basis or cited financial estimate is supplied for the loss amount. The contract records that basis as unknown.
criteria.support_condition: The broad construction-failure condition is established, and consistent financial records demonstrate at least US$200 billion of unrecovered investment caused by that failure, with a substantial portion financed through private credit linked to pension, retirement, and insurance capital.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the construction-failure condition is established and recoveries are sufficiently settled, comprehensive records establish aggregate losses below US$200 billion or show that the claimed substantial private-credit funding connection does not hold.

evidence.explanation: This supports the general connection between private credit and pension or insurance capital while qualifying the scale of aggregate exposure. It does not identify losses on failed AI data-center projects.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Definitive failure records for the relevant build-out, followed by consistent records of deployed capital and recoveries that settle whether losses reach US$200 billion. Financing records must trace the same losses through private credit to pension, retirement, and insurance investors without double counting.
